title: Guitar and banjo versus piano; amplified guitars
summary: Garland prefers guitar or banjo with violin, bass and drums in the seven-man band, and says amplifiers drown everything.

story.theme_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section: instruments and players
story.community_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section's changing role

blocks.x: Do you like to play with guitar players better than pianists, or do you like the piano better than the guitar?
Oh well I like the guitar. I like banjo.
Uh-huh.
You see years ago when banjo just started playing banjos, you know used to be five string banjo, but when they started six string banjo, you understand, the players always thought they was too noisy.
Yeah.
You see we used to use guitar in the band.
Right.
We use a violin -- so there's seven-men. That was the leader.
Uh-huh.
You use violin, guitar, bass, and drums, that was your rhythm section.
Yeah.
See? Four in the rhythm.
Uh-huh.
And the other three was trumpet, clarinet and trombone.
Yeah, did you like to play softer and easier with the guitar?
Oh, yes. And we would get that -- Bud Scott used to play with us.
Yes.
Play that guitar. But nowadays, they -- not they put the watchacallit, the -- amplifiers --
Yeah.
Some of them they don't know how to tune them up and they drown out everything, just like on the bass --
Yeah.
They tune them things up and they so loud, you understand?
Uh-huh.
They don't know how to tune the thing up.
